human_message:
BEACN voted NO because this was a large treasury withdrawal with incomplete budget, risk, and synthesis evidence. The proposal may support useful Cardano infrastructure, but treasury spending requires a higher evidence bar, and that bar was not met.

The action requested 540,750 ada for 12 months of Oura by TxPipe maintenance, submitted by Intersect on behalf of TxPipe. The proposal described a part-time maintainer, dependency updates, Cardano protocol compatibility, performance improvements, bug fixing, documentation, community support, and AI-friendly integration resources. It also stated that the withdrawal included 525,000 ada for maintenance and enhancement plus a 15,750 ada Intersect administration fee.

Several claims were supported: Oura’s basic technical role as an event pipeline was supported, the requested funding structure was supported in the proposal, the anchor document was available, the action passed the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting threshold, and the requested amount did not breach the applicable Net Change Limit at submission. But important claims were not independently supported, including prior Project Catalyst funding for Oura and TxPipe’s wider Catalyst delivery record. More importantly, the treasury review was incomplete: the assessment was missing a line-item budget, full budget analysis, feasibility assessment, risk analysis, alternatives analysis, failure-mode analysis, and community impact analysis.

The review gates reflected that weakness. Claims and evidence were thin, treasury analysis was incomplete, risk review was thin, and synthesis was blocked. BEACN’s review also noted an incomplete treasury diligence dossier, an unsustainable treasury flow signal, unknown execution risk, and a flag score that reduced confidence. For a treasury action consuming shared ada, those unresolved gaps outweighed the strongest YES case, so BEACN voted NO.

model_layer.note: Claim extraction and the plain-language message are model-assisted, advisory layers. The hard gates (stale data, missing evidence, treasury-needs-dossier, hard blockers, high flags) are deterministic and binding. The doctrine-aware reasoning layer may apply a bounded score nudge of at most ±0.05, clamped and recorded here (raw_score + llm_score_adjustment), so its influence is fully auditable and replayable.
